newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon sentences Japanese Red Army guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon sentences Japanese Red Army guerrillas.

text.p: A Lebanese court on Thursday sentenced five Japanese Red Army guerrillas to three years each in jail for a variety of charges relating to their illegal stay in the country.
The four men and one woman, who had been arrested in Beirut in February, were not brought to the court to hear the verdicts and sentences announced.
The five were convicted on different charges, including forging official stamps, illegal entry into Lebanon and forging passports, but all received the same three-year sentences.

The prisoners included Kozo Okamoto, who joined two comrades in a 1972 machinegun and grenade attack inside Tel Aviv's Lod airport that killed 26 people. He was captured but released by Israel in a 1985 prisoner exchange.

Okamoto and Haruo Wako received only jail sentences. Masao Adachi, Mariko Yamamoto and Kazuo Tohira were also fined 600,000 Lebanese pounds ($390). The judge said the prisoners, whom Japan had sought to put on trial, would be deported after their sentences. He did not say where they might go.

The court rejected the defence that their crimes in Lebanon had been political. "The motive was a personal and selfish interest that would allow them to stay in Lebanon regardless of their beliefs, though the court appreciates the heroic act one of the defendants (Okamoto) executed against the Israeli enemy," the judge said.
